review_findings.description: The quoteLinkParam function had a bug where the regex /["\\]/g only matched double quotes and backslashes, but the switch statement attempted to handle \r and \n characters which would never be matched. This caused control characters in header values to not be escaped, leading to potential header injection vulnerabilities and ERR_INVALID_CHAR errors when setting headers.

The formatLink function did not validate that descriptor objects have an href or url property. When neither was provided, it would produce invalid output like '<undefined>; rel="..."' which is not a valid Link header value.
The formatLink function did not validate input types. Non-string, non-URL, non-object values (like numbers) would be converted to strings and wrapped in angle brackets, producing invalid output.

blue_fix.fix_explanation: Fixed three issues in the PR implementation: 1) Updated quoteLinkParam regex to /["\\\r\n]/g to properly match and escape carriage returns and newlines in addition to quotes and backslashes. 2) Added validation in formatLink to throw TypeError when descriptor objects lack href/url properties. 3) Added validation in formatLink to throw TypeError when link values are not strings, URLs, or descriptor objects. These changes ensure proper header value escaping per RFC 7230 and prevent invalid Link header generation.
